label: 0059 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over 53 windows): Japan Trench coupling at most 1, with a sheet beneath the slab, extended seaward and down-dip, for relaxation beneath the subducting plate, uncorrelated noise, background coupling from −1 to 1, fourteen slow slip events as signal, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: The Japan Trench interface's total coupling, every state included, is held to at most 1. The near-trench seafloor's landward motion after Tohoku comes instead from a sheet beneath the slab, standing in for the boundary conditions that viscoelastic relaxation beneath the subducting plate imposes on it (as in Tomita et al., 2026, Science). The sheet is the Japan Trench mesh moved 20 km down, extended 50 km seaward of the trench at 20 km depth, beneath the incoming plate, and 50 km down-dip along the slab. Its Tohoku state is dip-slip only, can only pull the overlying plate landward, and has a prior of 300 mm/yr (one pattern, Omori decay with c = 1 yr). The Tohoku University frame velocity is estimated about the G14–MYGI tie as in 0058. The sheet carries about 150 mm/yr of slip deficit in 2012–2021 beneath the trench off Miyagi, up to 210 mm/yr just seaward of the main rupture, and much less elsewhere. Held-out seafloor sites are predicted better than by any earlier model (cross-validation +1,340, against +1,270 for 0058), and held-out onshore windows slightly worse (+407 against +532). The Tohoku University frame offset is −22 mm/yr (0058: −14.5), and shallow coupling off Miyagi averages 0.54 in 2012–2021, so the interface there is not fully relocked. Seafloor data: Japan Coast Guard (CC BY-NC 4.0) and Tohoku University (CC BY 4.0).
